facts.statement: Fragmentary remains of Boreonykus were discovered in the 1980s at the Pipestone Creek site in central Alberta while excavating a bonebed of the ceratopsid Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai.
facts.quote: Fragmentary dromaeosaurid remains were discovered in the 1980s at the Pipestone Creek site in central Alberta during excavations of a bonebed containing at least twenty-seven individuals of the ceratopsid Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai.

facts.statement: Remains initially attributed to Boreonykus were partly referred to Saurornitholestes sp. in 2001.
facts.quote: They were initially partly referred to a Saurornitholestes sp in 2001.

facts.statement: The genus name Boreonykus is a variation of "Boreonychus", meaning "northern claw".
facts.quote: The genus name is a variation of "Boreonychus", "northern claw".

facts.statement: The specific name certekorum honors the Certek company, which provided financial support for the excavations.
facts.quote: The specific name certekorum references the Certek company, that works in the oil industry and provided financial support for the excavations.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen TMP 1989.055.0047 was found in the Wapiti Formation in central Alberta and dates to the late Campanian, approximately 73.27 ± 0.25 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Boreonykus, TMP 1989.055.0047, was found in a layer of the Wapiti Formation in central Alberta, which dates from the late Campanian, 73.27 ± 0.25 million years ago.

facts.statement: The species is known from a right frontal bone, fourteen loose teeth, and several postcranial bones including a rear caudal vertebra, a second finger claw, and a foot sickle claw.
facts.quote: It consists of a right frontal bone. Fourteen loose teeth have been referred to the species, as well as several postcranial bones, perhaps of the same individual: the specimen TMP 1988.055.0129, a rear caudal vertebra; UALVP 53597, a claw of the second finger, and the specimen TMP 1986.055.0184.1, a sickle claw of the foot.

facts.statement: Boreonykus was originally classified in the subfamily Velociraptorinae but was recovered within Dromaeosaurinae in 2021.
facts.quote: Boreonykus was, within the Dromaeosauridae, placed in the Velociraptorinae. It was seen as both an indication of faunal provincialism and a quick species turn-over rate. However, in 2021, Boreonykus was recovered within the Dromaeosaurinae, restricting the distribution of velociraptorines only to Asia.

facts.statement: Boreonykus lived approximately 73 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió hace aproximadamente 73 million years ago, durante el Campaniense del Cretácico Superioren lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Boreonykus certekorum is the only known species of the extinct genus Boreonykus, a dromaeosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Boreonykus certekorum ("garra del norte de Certek Heating Solutions") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Boreonykus de dinosaurios celurosaurios dromeosáuridos

facts.statement: The genus name is a variation of "Boreonychus" (northern claw), a name previously used for a fictional dinosaur in an alternative evolution scenario.
facts.quote: El nombre del género es una variación de "Boreonychus", "garra del norte", cuyo nombre fue utilizado para un dinosaurio imaginario en un escenario de una evolución alternativa.

facts.statement: The suffix "onykus" in the name is confusing as it erroneously suggests a relationship to Alvarezsauridae.
facts.quote: La última parte del nombre, "onykus" es algo confusa, ya que erróneamente sugiere que pertenece a Alvarezsauridae, ya que esa terminación de nombre es común en los géneros pertenecientes a ese grupo.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen TMP 1989.055.0047 was found in the Wapiti Formation in central Alberta, Canada, dating to the late Campanian approximately 73.27 ± 0.25 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, TMP 1989.055.0047 de Boreonykus fue encontrado en una capa de la Formación Wapiti en el centro de Alberta, Canadá, que data de finales del Campaniense de hace 73.27 ± 0.25 millones de años.

facts.statement: The species is known from a right frontal bone, parts of the postcranium, and fourteen isolated teeth, including a rear caudal vertebra, a second finger claw, and two sickle claws of the foot.
facts.quote: Consiste principalmente en un hueso frontal derecho, además se han encontrado partes del postcráneo y catorce dientes aislados que fueron referidos a la especie; el espécimen TMP 1988.055.0129, incluye una vértebra caudal posterior; UALVP 53 597, una garra de la mano del segundo dedo, y dos garras del pie en forma de hoz incluidas en el espécimen TMP 1986.055.0184.

facts.statement: Only one autapomorphy was identified: ridges bordering the supratemporal fenestrae form an acute angle of 55° pointing backward.
facts.quote: Solo se identificó una autapomorfia, o rasgo único derivado: las crestas que bordean los frentes de las depresiones alrededor de la fenestra supratemporal forman un ángulo agudo de 55°, apuntando hacia atrás.

facts.statement: Boreonykus was classified within the subfamily Velociraptorinae, an indication of regional faunal differentiation and a rapid species turnover rate.
facts.quote: Boreonykus fue clasificado, dentro de la familia Dromaeosauridae, en la subfamilia Velociraptorinae. Esto se considera como una indicación tanto de la diferenciación regional de faunas como de una rápida tasa de reemplazo de especies.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Boreonykus as Dromaeosaurinae.
The time range for Boreonykus is recorded as Campanian to Campanian, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
